assumptions: Tag names 'personal', 'retained' and 'erasure' are what the customer would adopt; none exist in the workspace (policies left unchanged)
The ask 'delete their stuff everywhere' means table coverage by an erasure-tagged function, which is the only checkable reading
'2 years' is the customer's intended retention period, written into the RET-002 statement as intent only
delete_user_account (called by DELETE /account) is the intended erasure function, but it is not tagged erasure and does not cover most personal tables
Severity high for the GDPR erasure policy is my choice; the customer did not say
confusions: Recipe 'Erase and expire personal data' says to write one function and tag it, but the recipe's words for erasure tags and the coverage rule's referenced_by.tags are not explained together: it was unclear whether the erasure function must be tagged in the workspace before any rule can run
The RET-002 template's fill example is tags ['retained'], but it is not stated whether the template's fill tag is a scope param (tags) or a referenced_by param; I used the scope param, which parsed
The catalogue limit 'the age lives in the task's own query' is stated, but no guidance says how to express a retention period as a policy (none exists); the statement had to carry it as intent

The parse warnings name missing tags as warnings, but the skill says not to accept warnings; I kept the rules with the tags the customer needs and proposed the tags instead of changing the workspace, which means both rules currently select nothing
wished_for: A check or param for record age / retention period (e.g. a db.bulk.delete where expires_at or created_at is older than N days)
A recipe or template for 'delete a user everywhere' that shows how to tag personal tables and the erasure function together
A check that verifies the erasure function deletes the records that identify the user (e.g. where user_id equals $input), not just that it deletes from the table
Guidance on whether a policy written before its tags exist should be published (it parses but selects nothing) or held until the tags are added
parse_errors_seen: RET-002.R1: tags "retained" is on no table on this branch, so it selects nothing (warning; parse exit 0)
GDPR-ERASURE.R1: tags "personal" is on no table on this branch, so it selects nothing (warning; parse exit 0)
GDPR-ERASURE.R1: referenced_by.tags "erasure" is on no function on this branch, so no object covers a table through it (warning; parse exit 0)
why_confidence: Both rules parse, but none of their tags exist, so as written they select nothing and check nothing until the customer tags tables and the erasure function. Even then, the erasure rule only checks table coverage, not that delete_user_account removes the right records, and it cannot see third-party copies or backups. The 2-year limit is not checkable at all: RET-002 only confirms a cleanup task exists. The workspace's delete_user_account currently misses most personal tables (orders, payments, support_tickets and others), so the rule would flag real gaps once tagged.
